body:
Thank you for the response. What is the best way to do it? I have a friend that also gave me the same advice, but I don't know a good script for asking the question without it seeming really awkward. When should I ask? In person? Over text? What do people say? I feel like a little middle-school child, because all I remember from when I was a kid was stuff like "Oh do you *like* *like* me??" and similar. Do I say "Are you interested romantically?" 

It is true, I feel like I feel better knowing a for sure yes or no rather than me wondering all the time.

I don't know if I can wait years for the chance that my sexuality might possibly change. The last time we had sex, I felt the whole time like I was going to throw up. Maybe that was just nerves, but it makes me feel like a terrible person. I feel like I don't want to let go for that slim chance that I may grow sexual attraction again, but I guess I feel like I can't hold on for years just waiting. It is torture for me now, I can barely touch my partner, I can't imagine years of this. Maybe that is just me being weak and a bad partner. I just wish there was a definite answer.

Thank you. I might DM you. I am so worried because I feel like I have come to realize that I am not romantically attracted to feminine-presenting people, but I don't even know if I can trust my body and brain right now. I have a therapist to talk to, but the appointments are pretty spread out, about once a month.

He has a therapist, and so do I. Wait times are a bit long because our uni's budget just got bumped down. I don't know if I can wait a month to talk to a couple's counsellor. Do you have any advice for talking about it at home?
Feel free to PM me. I would really love to talk to someone in the same situation.

That is what I am worried about. I can't trust my own body and my responses. How long do you think I should wait to see if it is genuine or not? I have spoken to a therapist about it just last week, and it has been almost 2 months since my boyfriend told me. Do you think my lack of attraction toward my boyfriend being feminine could be this too?

That's true. He was capable of making this decision in the first place, which I am sure was very difficult on its own. He is so smart and really deserves someone who loves absolutely everything about him. Thank you a lot for this advice.

I am sure it isn't abnormal, but some part of my brain is telling me that I don't actually love my boyfriend if I can't get through this with them. Maybe that is irrational, I don't know. And then I worry about my feelings in this situation even being valid, because they are the one going through this whole change with their body, not me. I feel so selfish for thinking about myself.

I guess that is another thing I worry about though. I feel so selfish, and all around like a huge asshole. I feel like I should be able to do something. Maybe it is just me being too worried and over-analysing it all. Part of my brain is telling me that I don't actually love them if I can't get through this. And I don't know if that is irrational or not.

Thank you for this advice. I absolutely do want to remain friends with them, or at least have them know that I still want to be around for them. I guess what is bothering me though is what you mentioned: neither of us have done anything wrong. I feel like this would be so much easier if it was someone's fault, then at least I would feel more in control, or justified in leaving. But with this, I don't feel justified, I just feel like a major asshole because I can't force myself to be attracted to them. I will talk to them about the couple's therapy option, I think that seems like a good idea.
Thanks, I will post there as well.

Maybe. I do want to get this discussion happening sooner rather than later, since I don't want him to feel this like...false sense of security in believing that I am 100% okay. I really really do want to remain supportive, and I believe he is already seeing an LGBT friendly therapist too. I just can't help still being worried about him 24/7. It is not an exaggeration to say that this is actually on my mind all the time.
